policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere עָלוּ (plural) vs ketiv עלה (singular) differ only in verb number; ASV 'the servants ... came up' has a plural subject with an English past tense that does not mark number, so the wording permits either reading. No note mapped. Base qere carries the projection.
Qere עֲשֶׂרֶת vs ketiv עשרה are gender forms of the same numeral 'ten'; ASV 'ten thousand' renders either identically. No note mapped. Base qere carries the projection.

Qere אֵילֵי vs ketiv אולי are both read 'chief/mighty men'; ASV 'the chief men of the land' fits either, and the notes 'Or, eunuchs' and 'Or, mighty' are alternative_rendering, which never decides a reading. Base qere carries the projection.

ASV wording 'Hamutal' transliterates the qere vocalisation חֲמוּטַל; the ketiv חמיטל would be 'Hamital', which the ASV relegates to its hebrew_gloss note 'Hebrew Hamital.' The text follows the qere, the note records the ketiv it did not print.
